profiled_workloads.selection_reason: Lowest eval speedup (1.309x) of all timing workloads; bf16 1024x3 = 3072 elements, the smallest-work regime whose speedup is the biggest geo_mean lever.
Boundary case of the flat regime: fp16 65536x3 = 196608 elements, 64x the work of timing-0/3 yet the same eval latency, so it tests whether the ~14 us floor is size-independent.

Highest eval latency (0.0707 ms), bf16 1048576x3 = 3145728 elements; same byte footprint and same 4096 tile as the fp16 1M case that is 17.9 us faster, so it isolates a dtype-dependent large-regime limit.

Strong control for timing-5: fp16 1048576x3 has identical element count, bytes and tile as the bf16 1M case but measures 0.0528 ms, so it separates a dtype/codegen limit from a bandwidth limit in the large regime.

performance_interpretation: Profiler evidence is absent this round, so every number below is from the authoritative eval snapshot in get_profile_context (eval_status PASSED, fingerprint 3b2bc0ec..., solution SHA b1404a3f106c...) and the evaluated source; none of it is profiler-confirmed and it must not be reported as a measured device bottleneck. (1) The frozen hypothesis (BLOCK 4096 for 4-byte elements above 131072 elements) is CONFIRMED by eval: cross_out-timing-8 (fp32 1048576x3) fell from 0.09305 to 0.06824 ms (-26.66%, speedup 12.229 -> 16.674); the same threshold also pushed cross_out-timing-7 (fp32 65536x3 = 196608 elements, above the cutoff) from 0.014010 to 0.015236 ms (+8.75%, speedup 7.335 -> 6.742). Net geo_mean 5.23916589100821 -> 5.4910608537908345 (+4.81%). (2) Six of nine timing workloads are size-invariant: timing-0 (fp16 3072 elements) 0.013940, timing-1 (fp16 196608) 0.013947, timing-3 (bf16 3072) 0.013973, timing-4 (bf16 196608) 0.013991, timing-6 (fp32 3072) 0.015329, timing-7 (fp32 196608) 0.015236 ms. A 64x work increase changes latency by ~0.01-0.15 us, so these cases sit on a fixed ~13.9 us floor rather than on work; the fp32 pair is ~1.3 us above the 2-byte pair at both sizes, indicating a small dtype-dependent term on top of that floor. Their speedup spread (1.31x-6.74x) is driven entirely by the reference cost, since candidate latency is identical. Whether that floor is candidate dispatch, device launch, or harness overhead is unresolved and is the single largest open lever, because six workloads are addressable at once if it is ours. (3) In the large regime the ordering is fp16 0.052790 < fp32 0.068240 < bf16 0.070704 ms with identical byte footprints for fp16/bf16 and identical tile constants, stable across rounds 4-5 (round 4: fp16 0.053315, bf16 0.071196). bf16 paying +34% over fp16 at equal bytes points to arithmetic/store dtype rather than traffic, but with no instruction listing this remains a hypothesis. (4) The flat kernel reads each input element about four times (four shifted streams per tensor, eight loads per tile), a deliberate replacement for the measured 0.41 ms/gather tl.gather shuffles; that amplification is a plausible large-regime cost but cannot be quantified without physical byte counters.

next_experiment.action_description: Do NOT sweep tiles again; the tile question is settled. First run one bounded Debug Job (<=120 s) that attributes the size-invariant ~13.9 us floor on the exact native input of cross_out-timing-3 (bf16 [1024,3], dim=-1) by timing, in this order: (a) the full candidate run() call in a warm repeat loop, (b) the cached raw launcher.launch call alone with the same grid/BLOCK/STEP, (c) a trivial no-op kernel launched with the identical grid and metadata. Decision rule: if (c) is within ~1-2 us of (a), the floor is launch/host-side and step 2 applies; if (c) is well below (a) (e.g. <=5 us), the floor is harness/device-fixed, abandon this branch and instead do step 3. Step 2 (only if the floor is ours): trim the per-call dispatch depth without changing semantics - cache a single bound launcher plus the resolved stream object at plan time instead of re-reading out.dtype/out.numel() properties and calling _current_stream() on every call, keep the existing pointer/numel/dtype identity recheck so a different tensor, resized out or re-allocated storage still falls back to the slow path, and keep the general ND path, alias protection, masks and NaN/Inf behaviour untouched. Step 3 (fallback): force the flat-kernel arithmetic into fp32 (upcast the eight loaded tiles, multiply/subtract in fp32, cast the result back before the masked store) to test whether the bf16 large case is limited by bf16 arithmetic rather than by traffic.
next_experiment.expected_impact: Step 1 is diagnostic and expected to change geo_mean by 0 us. If the floor is candidate-side and drops from ~13.9 us to ~11 us, the six floor workloads (timing-0/-1/-3/-4/-6/-7) move by roughly 1.27x each (1.316x for the fp32 pair) and the headline geo_mean rises about +19% from 5.4911 toward ~6.5. If the bf16 fp32-math branch works instead, cross_out-timing-5 moves from 0.07070 toward the fp16 0.05279 ms level, i.e. speedup 16.56 -> ~22.2, worth about +3.3% geo_mean.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: Step 2 risks: a cached stream object can go stale across stream/device changes, and a cached launcher must not reuse a first-call scalar or pointer (the known xlogy failure mode in this workspace). Mitigate by caching only the compiled function/metadata and the resolved stream, never tensor pointers or sizes, and by keeping the existing per-call identity recheck. Both steps must preserve in-place/out aliasing, stride, broadcast, NaN/Inf and current-stream semantics. Rollback: the round-5 source is frozen at solution SHA b1404a3f106c901bd46e2c4a4372e96c8070b2ac3632a5da6e9739ff2ad12022 with eval fingerprint 3b2bc0ec...; if either branch regresses geo_mean below 5.4910608537908345 or breaks any correctness workload, revert to that file verbatim. Do not relax the 131072 tile threshold or re-tune BLOCK as part of this experiment, so the measurement stays single-factor.
